Tie-breaking favors the deterministic policy as it is typically more predictable and resource-efficient.\\n\\n**Contrast with Step-Level Oracle Routing (e.g., ITP-R):**\\n\\nStep-level oracles attempt to assign credit at each decision step $t$:\\n\\n$$L_{\\\\text{step}}(e, t) = \\\\arg\\\\max_{\\\\pi} \\\\mathbb{E}[R_t \\\\mid \\\\pi, s_t]$$\\n\\nIn environments with sparse terminal reward (e.g., ScienceWorld gives score only at episode end), this requires per-step credit assignment which degenerates:\\n\\n$$\\\\text{Var}[\\\\hat{L}_{\\\\text{step}}(e, t)] \\\\to \\\\infty \\\\quad \\\\text{as reward sparsity increases}$$\\n\\nOur episode-level protocol avoids this entirely by operating on the final outcome.\\n\\n*Evidence:* ScienceWorld provides only terminal scores; step-level approaches cannot attribute signal to intermediate steps without auxiliary reward shaping.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 1.2 Death Avoidance Fraction (DAF)\\n\\n**Definition: Death Episode.** An episode $e$ is a *death episode* under policy $\\\\pi_{\\\\text{int}}$ if:\\n\\n$$\\\\text{Death}(e) \\\\iff S_{\\\\text{int}}(e) = 0$$\\n\\ni.e., the internal/generative policy achieves catastrophic failure (zero score).\\n\\n**Episode Partitions (over all episodes):**\\n\\n$$\\\\mathcal{E}_{\\\\text{death}} = \\\\{e \\\\in \\\\mathcal{E} : \\\\text{Death}(e)\\\\}, \\\\quad \\\\mathcal{E}_{\\\\text{nd}} = \\\\{e \\\\in \\\\mathcal{E} : \\\\neg\\\\text{Death}(e)\\\\}$$\\n\\n**Full Routing Signal (all episodes):**\\n\\n$$\\\\Delta_{\\\\text{full}} = \\\\frac{1}{N} \\\\sum_{i=1}^{N} \\\\left[ S_{\\\\text{det}}(e_i) - S_{\\\\text{int}}(e_i) \\\\right]$$\\n\\nwhere $N = |\\\\mathcal{E}|$ is the total number of episodes.\\n\\n**Non-Death Routing Signal (all non-death episodes):**\\n\\n$$\\\\Delta_{\\\\text{nd}} = \\\\frac{1}{|\\\\mathcal{E}_{\\\\text{nd}}|} \\\\sum_{e \\\\in \\\\mathcal{E}_{\\\\text{nd}}} \\\\left[ S_{\\\\text{det}}(e) - S_{\\\\text{int}}(e) \\\\right]$$\\n\\n**Death Avoidance Fraction:**\\n\\n$$\\\\text{DAF} = 1 - \\\\frac{\\\\Delta_{\\\\text{nd}}}{\\\\Delta_{\\\\text{full}}}$$\\n\\n*Intuition:* DAF measures how much the overall routing signal diminishes when death episodes are removed. If $\\\\text{DAF} \\\\approx 1$, removing death episodes eliminates nearly all routing signal—meaning the routing advantage is essentially death avoidance. ## Part 1: Formal Definitions

### 1.1 Episode-Level Counterfactual Labeling Protocol

**Setup.** Let $E$ be a sequential decision-making environment, $\Pi = \{\pi_{\text{det}}, \pi_{\text{int}}\}$ a set of two execution policies (deterministic/tool-use and internal/generative), and $\mathcal{E} = \{e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_N\}$ a set of episodes (tasks).

**Counterfactual Execution.** For each episode $e \in \mathcal{E}$, execute both policies to obtain:

$$S_{\text{det}}(e) = \text{Score}(e, \pi_{\text{det}}), \quad S_{\text{int}}(e) = \text{Score}(e, \pi_{\text{int}})$$

where $\text{Score}: \mathcal{E} \times \Pi \to [0, 1]$ is the environment's normalized evaluation metric.

**Oracle Label Function:**

$$L(e) = \begin{cases} \pi_{\text{det}} & \text{if } S_{\text{det}}(e) > S_{\text{int}}(e) \\ \pi_{\text{int}} & \text{if } S_{\text{int}}(e) > S_{\text{det}}(e) \\ \pi_{\text{det}} & \text{if } S_{\text{det}}(e) = S_{\text{int}}(e) \quad \text{(tie-breaking: prefer deterministic)} \end{cases}$$

*Intuition:* The label function answers "which policy would have been better for this episode?" by actually running both and comparing. Tie-breaking favors the deterministic policy as it is typically more predictable and resource-efficient.

**Contrast with Step-Level Oracle Routing (e.g., ITP-R):**

Step-level oracles attempt to assign credit at each decision step $t$:

$$L_{\text{step}}(e, t) = \arg\max_{\pi} \mathbb{E}[R_t \mid \pi, s_t]$$

In environments with sparse terminal reward (e.g., ScienceWorld gives score only at episode end), this requires per-step credit assignment which degenerates:

$$\text{Var}[\hat{L}_{\text{step}}(e, t)] \to \infty \quad \text{as reward sparsity increases}$$

Our episode-level protocol avoids this entirely by operating on the final outcome.

*Evidence:* ScienceWorld provides only terminal scores; step-level approaches cannot attribute signal to intermediate steps without auxiliary reward shaping.

---

### 1.2 Death Avoidance Fraction (DAF)

**Definition: Death Episode.** An episode $e$ is a *death episode* under policy $\pi_{\text{int}}$ if:

$$\text{Death}(e) \iff S_{\text{int}}(e) = 0$$

i.e., the internal/generative policy achieves catastrophic failure (zero score).

**Episode Partitions (over all episodes):**

$$\mathcal{E}_{\text{death}} = \{e \in \mathcal{E} : \text{Death}(e)\}, \quad \mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}} = \{e \in \mathcal{E} : \neg\text{Death}(e)\}$$

$$\Delta_{\text{full}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ S_{\text{det}}(e_i) - S_{\text{int}}(e_i) \right]$$

where $N = |\mathcal{E}|$ is the total number of episodes.

**Non-Death Routing Signal (all non-death episodes):**

$$\Delta_{\text{nd}} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}}|} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}}} \left[ S_{\text{det}}(e) - S_{\text{int}}(e) \right]$$

**Death Avoidance Fraction:**

$$\text{DAF} = 1 - \frac{\Delta_{\text{nd}}}{\Delta_{\text{full}}}$$

*Intuition:* DAF measures how much the overall routing signal diminishes when death episodes are removed. Computed over ALL episodes (not just the det-preferred subset). - $\text{DAF} = 0$: Routing signal is fully preserved after removing death episodes. $\Delta_{\text{nd}} = \Delta_{\text{full}}$.

## 1. Framework 核心 Formalization

### Episode-level Counterfactual Labeling Protocol

- Environment $E$, policy set $\Pi = \{\pi_{\text{det}}, \pi_{\text{int}}\}$, episode set $\mathcal{E} = \{e_1, \ldots, e_N\}$
- Counterfactual execution: run both policies on every episode, obtain $S_{\text{det}}(e)$ and $S_{\text{int}}(e)$
- Oracle label $\ell(e) \in \{\texttt{det-pref}, \texttt{int-pref}, \texttt{no-pref}\}$ (three-way: death asymmetry → surviving strategy preferred; both dead or tied alive → no-preference)
- Key advantage over step-level oracle (e.g., ITP-R): works with sparse terminal reward, no per-step credit assignment needed

### Death Avoidance Fraction (DAF) — All-Episodes Definition

**Death indicator:** $d(\tau) \in \{0, 1\}$ for each trajectory; $d=1 \Rightarrow s(\tau) = -P$. Both $d(\tau_{\text{int}})$ and $d(\tau_{\text{det}})$ are recorded independently.

**Episode partitions (over ALL episodes):**
$$\mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}} = \{e \in \mathcal{E} : d(\tau_{\text{det}})=0 \wedge d(\tau_{\text{int}})=0\}$$

**Full routing signal (all N episodes):**
$$\Delta_{\text{full}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ S_{\text{det}}(e_i) - S_{\text{int}}(e_i) \right]$$

**Non-death routing signal (both-survive episodes):**
$$\Delta_{\text{nd}} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}}|} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{nd}}} \left[ S_{\text{det}}(e) - S_{\text{int}}(e) \right]$$

**DAF:**
$$\text{DAF} = 1 - \frac{\Delta_{\text{nd}}}{\Delta_{\text{full}}}$$

Intuition: how much the overall routing signal drops when death episodes are removed. Computed over ALL episodes, not just det-preferred.
